title: Contract Pricing Agreement Rebate Forfeiture: Period Alignment Relief
content:
## Period alignment relief — Contract Pricing Agreement rebate forfeiture

The alignment relief follows where the termination effective date sits in the rebate period in which the termination took effect, measured against the date of the agreement's latest accrual. The relief is subtracted from the termination period's net rebate before the forfeiture's floor at 0.00 and its rounding to the cent are applied.

1. A termination effective on the period's last day, so that the latest accrual is dated the next day, takes 0.05 times the termination period's net rebate.
2. A termination effective on one of the 31 days before the date of the latest accrual other than the period's last day takes 0.025 times the termination period's net rebate.
3. An earlier termination takes no alignment relief.

Calendar days from one date to another count the later date and not the earlier one. Wherever a latest record of a kind is taken, it is the one with the latest date, and among records of the same date the one recorded first.

| Termination effective date, days before the latest accrual date | Alignment relief |
|---|---|
| 1 (the period's last day) | 0.05 times the net rebate |
| 2 | 0.025 times the net rebate |
| 31 | 0.025 times the net rebate |
| 32 or more | None |

Hypothetical example: on a net rebate of 800.00, a termination effective on the quarter's last day takes 40.00; one effective ten days before the accrual date takes 20.00.
